headline_fact: Chickpeas, sesame and careful blending turn a few ingredients into a creamy dip.
summary: Meet hummus, understand its texture, and make an Indian-kitchen adaptation.
did_you_know: Blending changes the texture without changing the basic ingredients.
core_mechanics: Soft chickpeas break down and blend with sesame paste and liquid.
why_it_matters: A familiar ingredient can introduce a different food tradition.

in_depth_breakdown.real_world_application: A trolley carrying more mass needs more net force to achieve the same acceleration.

learning_takeaways: Texture depends on soft chickpeas and enough liquid.

food_lesson.hook: Chickpeas, sesame and careful blending turn a few ingredients into a creamy dip.
food_lesson.question: How do chickpeas become a smooth, rich dip?
food_lesson.learning_goal: Understand what each ingredient does, then make a simple version at home.

introduction.explanation: Hummus combines cooked chickpeas with tahini, lemon juice and water. The result is a thick dip that people scoop with bread or eat with other dishes. This lesson uses a small batch to show how texture changes during blending.
introduction.how_it_is_served: Serve it in a shallow bowl alongside bread, vegetables or a larger meal. A spoonful can also add richness to a plate of roasted vegetables.
introduction.why_it_is_interesting: Its appeal comes from a balance of earthy chickpeas, rich sesame and bright lemon. The preparation shows how soft ingredients and a little liquid can create a smooth texture.

origin_and_context.explanation: Hummus belongs to several food traditions across the Levant. Recipes and ways of serving it vary between households and places.
origin_and_context.regional_variation: Some versions are looser or more lemony. Garnishes and accompaniments also vary.
origin_and_context.uncertainty: A shared food tradition does not have one simple, universally agreed account of its origin.

sensory_profile.flavour: Earthy chickpeas, nutty sesame and a bright lemon finish.
sensory_profile.aroma: A mild sesame aroma; lemon adds a fresh note.
sensory_profile.texture: Smooth and thick enough to scoop, rather than stiff or dry.
sensory_profile.heat: The base recipe is mild. Chilli is an optional variation.
sensory_profile.serving_temperature: Usually enjoyed cool or at room temperature, depending on the preparation.

key_ingredients.name: Chickpeas
key_ingredients.role: The cooked chickpeas provide most of the structure.
key_ingredients.effect_on_taste: They give the dip its mild, earthy base.

key_ingredients.name: Tahini
key_ingredients.role: Sesame paste adds fat and helps create a rich texture.
key_ingredients.effect_on_taste: Its nutty flavour balances the lemon.

food_science.title: Soft chickpeas blend more smoothly
food_science.explanation: Blending breaks the cooked chickpeas into smaller pieces. Firm chickpeas leave more noticeable particles. Enough liquid lets the mixture move through the blender instead of sticking around the blades.
food_science.kitchen_cue: A spoon should leave a soft groove, and the mixture should spread without crumbling.

recipe.title: A small batch of hummus
recipe.traditional_preparation: The familiar chickpea version uses chickpeas, tahini and lemon. Exact proportions and additions vary.
recipe.adaptation_notes: Use well-cooked kabuli chana and a mixer-grinder. This is an illustrative home-kitchen adaptation; it is not presented as the only traditional recipe.

ingredients.name: Cooked chickpeas
ingredients.preparation: Drain; use chickpeas that crush easily.

ingredients.name: Tahini
ingredients.preparation: Stir the sesame paste before measuring.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.preparation: Keep extra water nearby for adjusting texture.

substitutions.quantity: Use 60 g of smooth sesame paste.
substitutions.effect: A home-ground paste may be coarser or stronger than commercial tahini. Keep the sesame allergen information unchanged.

steps.title: Combine the sesame and lemon
steps.instruction: Place the tahini and lemon juice in the blender. Add half the water and blend briefly.
steps.time_guidance: Blend for about 30 seconds, pausing if needed.
steps.doneness_cue: The paste looks evenly mixed, with no separate lemon juice.

steps.title: Add the chickpeas
steps.instruction: Add the chickpeas and salt. Blend, pause and scrape the sides. Add the remaining measured water gradually.
steps.time_guidance: Blend in short bursts for about 2–3 minutes.
steps.doneness_cue: The dip moves around the blades and looks mostly smooth.

steps.title: Check the texture
steps.instruction: Spoon the dip into a bowl. Taste and check whether it spreads easily. If it is too thick, add water a little at a time.
steps.time_guidance: Allow about 2 minutes for checking and adjusting.
steps.doneness_cue: A spoon makes a soft groove without the dip looking dry.

allergens: Sesame, including the suggested sesame-paste substitute.
safety_notes: Stop and unplug the mixer before reaching near the blades or scraping around them.

nutrition_context.explanation: Chickpeas contribute protein and fibre, while sesame adds fat and richness. The whole meal and the amount eaten matter more than assigning the dip a health score.
nutrition_context.tradeoffs: A larger serving also provides more energy. Garnishes and extra oil change its composition.
nutrition_context.portion_context: The example recipe makes four small portions to accompany other foods.
nutrition_context.serving_basis: One of four portions of the example recipe.
assumptions: No numerical estimates are supplied for this demonstration recipe.

serving_ideas.title: Add contrasting textures
serving_ideas.explanation: Pair the smooth dip with crunchy vegetables or bread. It can accompany a meal rather than replace every other part of it.

variations.name: A more lemon-forward version
variations.difference: More lemon changes the acidity and may require a small adjustment to the liquid.

troubleshooting.cause: The chickpeas may still be too firm, or the mixture may be too dry to circulate.
troubleshooting.fix: Use softer cooked chickpeas and adjust the water gradually before blending again.

takeaways: Texture depends on soft chickpeas and enough liquid.
